hero.lead: Execution, routing, research, and portfolio management across 45 chains, from one venue. Trade through Terminal or Telegram, or integrate through REST, MCP, and typed SDKs.

interfaces.title: One account. Every surface.
interfaces.lead: The interface changes what can be authorized. We keep those authority boundaries visible instead of implying feature parity.
interfaces.boundary: REST supports managed execution and unsigned self-custody flows. MCP’s execute_swap prepares an unsigned transaction and does not broadcast it; A2A is limited to discovery and quoting.

execution.title: Intent becomes an execution you can inspect.
execution.lead: Routing and authority are separate. After quoting, you can optionally run a zero-funds preflight before the separate authorization decision.
execution.intentBody: Specify amount, assets, source, and destination. Nothing has moved yet.
execution.quoteBody: Eligible venues depend on the requested chains and pair; the response exposes the selected route.
execution.simulateBody: The Agent API can dry-run the proposed swap and safety checks without signing or moving funds.
execution.authorizeBody: Self-custody returns an unsigned transaction for you to sign. Managed REST execution can sign and broadcast under server-side controls.
execution.screenshotAlt: Suwappu Terminal showing an ETH/USDC chart, order book, and swap ticket.
execution.mevBody: A Rust-based searcher screens pending routes for sandwich risk before execution, in-house rather than outsourced.
execution.benchBody: Every execution path is benchmarked against measured latency and slippage, not simulated numbers.

proof.mobileHint: Product screenshot. On narrow screens, scroll horizontally to inspect full-size interface detail.

markets.title: Routing ranks every venue before you see a quote.
markets.crossChainBody: The platform inventory lists {platformChains} chains while the Agent API exposes {agentApiChains}. A quote only uses venues compatible with that route.
markets.hyperliquidBody: HyperLiquid trading is available through Suwappu product surfaces; programmatic capabilities depend on the specific Agent API or MCP tool.
markets.tempoBody: Tempo support is not uniform across interfaces. The current Agent API exposes Tempo token discovery, but Agent API swap execution on Tempo is not enabled.
markets.curveBody: The terminal's Curve venue lists every pool on every chain Curve deploys to, straight from the Curve Prices API, sortable by TVL, 24h volume, or base APR, searchable, and one click from the swap desk. Built on our fork of flet-curve.
markets.screenshotAlt: Suwappu perps desk showing HyperLiquid markets, market data, and an order ticket.
markets.screenshotCaption: HyperLiquid perps inside Suwappu · product capture · 31 Jul 2026
markets.lead: Smart route priority orders venues, including Tempo's enshrined DEX for zero-fee stable swaps and CoW's MEV-protected batch auctions, before CCTP and Across settle a bridge leg. A failover RPC manager keeps every one of the 45 chains routable if a provider degrades.

security.title: Execution moves value. Authority stays explicit.
security.lead: Choose self-custody or managed signing, then constrain what an automated key is allowed to do.
security.selfCustodyBody: Unsigned transaction flows keep signing and broadcasting with the caller, nothing server-side ever holds that key.
security.managedBody: Managed execution signs through KMS envelope encryption (kms_aesgcm_v2), Turnkey TEE signing, or an MPC signer, depending on the wallet path.
security.policiesBody: 2FA, spending limits, circuit breakers, and social recovery are enforced at the server boundary; approval monitoring auto-revokes what it flags.
security.boundaryBody: This page does not claim SOC 2 certification or a completed public third-party protocol audit. The security page documents current controls and limitations.

faq.title: The practical questions, answered plainly.
faq.coverageQuestion: What does the platform actually cover?
faq.coverageAnswer: The generated inventory lists {platformChains} platform chains and {routerCount} integrated routing venues. Routing is chain-gated, and the Agent API currently exposes {agentApiChains} chains.
faq.venuesQuestion: Do all {routerCount} venues compete for every quote?
faq.venuesAnswer: No. Venue support varies by chain and route. Suwappu evaluates the compatible subset and exposes the selected route.
faq.authorityAnswer: Self-custody flows return unsigned transactions for the caller to sign. Managed REST execution can sign and broadcast through a managed wallet under server-side controls.
faq.interfacesQuestion: Do REST, MCP, and A2A have the same authority?
faq.interfacesAnswer: No. REST includes managed and self-custody execution paths. MCP’s execute_swap prepares an unsigned transaction and does not broadcast it. A2A stops at discovery and quoting.

close.title: Send intent. Keep execution authority explicit.
close.lead: Start with the interface that matches who should review, sign, and broadcast.

research.title: Research and signals, published in the open.
research.lead: Signals run in the Terminal and over the API. Research goes out the same way: dated, attributed, and public.
research.launchBody: The launch detector watches Pump.fun and Raydium and flags new tokens the moment they deploy.
research.hlBody: Trades, funding, and liquidations across the HyperLiquid ecosystem, watched continuously.
research.dataBody: Real-time pricing and on-chain monitoring feed the signals API and every chart in the Terminal.

portfolio.title: Portfolio management for a position that spans chains.
portfolio.lead: Positions roll up across every chain the terminal trades, into one book you can read at a glance. A weekly digest recaps performance.
portfolio.positionsBody: One positions service aggregates holdings across every supported chain, no per-chain bookkeeping.
portfolio.pnlBody: PnL is computed per position and rolled into a single equity curve in the Terminal.
portfolio.cardsBody: A position can mint an on-chain receipt: a position card that travels with the trade.

government.title: The government arm: post-quantum by design.
government.lead: The Lattice Transfer Protocol handles post-quantum data transfer with on-chain anchors, built toward FedRAMP High readiness.
government.pqBody: Standard mode uses ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) key encapsulation, ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) signatures, and BLAKE3 content addressing.
government.provenBody: Lean 4 proofs cover quorum safety, constant-size sealed keys, and erasure thresholds, gated in CI.
government.fedrampBody: An evidence package with a NIST SP 800-53 control crosswalk and a fail-closed government deployment profile.
